entities.summary: The Mark Hellinger Theatre is a theater and church building at 237 West 51st Street in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City, U.S. Opened in 1930, the Hellinger Theatre is named after journalist Mark Hellinger and was developed by Warner Bros. as a movie palace before later hosting Broadway productions. It was designed by Thomas W. Lamb with a 1930s–modern style facade and a Baroque interior. It has 1,603 seats across two levels and has been a house of worship for the Times Square Church since 1989. Both the exterior and interior of the theater are New York City landmarks.
